mapping_rationale: MFA for privileged and non-privileged users plus authenticator management and risk-triggered re-authentication
Authoritative identifiers and account lifecycle feed every policy decision
Flag atypical account use and feed identity risk into the access decision
Least privilege with dynamic privilege management instead of standing admin rights
Baselines and settings checked continuously so posture can gate access
You cannot evaluate a device you have not inventoried; supplier risk covers what arrives pre-compromised
Device identity and health become inputs to access for managed and unmanaged endpoints
Endpoint detection and integrity checks supply real-time device risk
Deny-by-default boundaries and partitioning limit lateral movement
Flows are permitted by application need and documented internal connections
Encrypt and authenticate all sessions including internal east-west traffic
Protected paths and enforcement points must stay available under failure or DoS
Per-application authorization with session limits instead of network-level trust
Inline protection and monitoring tuned to application-layer attacks
Apps are reachable through policy enforcement points without a full-tunnel VPN
Signed components and controlled pipelines keep workload integrity verifiable
Continuous testing produces evidence of workload security posture
Data stores are resources and must be located before they can be protected
Sensitivity labels become attributes the policy engine can evaluate
Backup and tested recovery keep data resources usable after an incident
Attribute-based least-privilege access to data rather than broad share permissions
Encryption at rest with managed keys protects data wherever it lives
Centralized logging and analysis supply the telemetry the trust algorithm relies on
Automated handling closes the loop between detection and enforcement
Risk strategy and performance measures keep the program accountable and repeatable
